category_title: Students who engage in gossiping and bystander behavior
minimal_context: The student is participating in an end-of-the-day debrief activity on the challenge course, passing a string to share reflections on preventing bullying.
dialogue:
TUTOR: We are starting our end-of-the-day debrief with the Human Web. Please take the string and complete the statement: 'To help prevent bullying, my hope for our school is . . . and I commit to . . .'

STUDENT: I'm not sure what to commit to. Before today, I thought like only me or one of my friends was the only person that was really getting hurt.

TUTOR: Think about the silent walk across the circle we did earlier. What did you notice then?

STUDENT: I saw that a lot of other people have been teased or called names. But like normally I am like afraid to do anything when I see someone being bullied.

TUTOR: What do you usually do in those situations?

STUDENT: Well usually if one of my friends starts saying bad stuff about a person I would just like go along with it. I end up just ignoring it because I don't know what else to do.

options.A: Employ visual or gestural prompts during the debrief activity while the student is holding the string in the circle of their peers.
options.B: Use strategies from play therapy to set behavioral boundaries during the debrief activity while maintaining a safe relationship with the student in the circle.
options.C: Terminate the current demands and remove the string and other debrief materials from the student for 10 seconds during the circle activity.
options.D: Prior to jumping off the platform for the zip line, ask the student to complete the sentence, 'When I zip off this platform, behaviors I am going to leave behind are . . .'
